Machine Learning for Cell Dynamics

In biomedicine, single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) measures the 
activity of thousands of genes in individual cells,
producing high-dimensional datasets that capture cellular diversity and 
transitions between cell states.
In this internship we aim to reconstruct a dynamical system from noisy 
snapshots of thousands of genes,
when the underlying biological processes are only partially observed.
The challenge is to compress these data into a low-dimensional 
representation while preserving
the structure of cell-state transitions, infer the stochastic dynamics 
governing these transitions,
and identify a small set of variables and interactions that explain the 
observed behaviour.
This requires going beyond standard prediction methods to build models 
that are both interpretable
and capable of predicting responses to perturbations.

The internship will develop machine-learning methods based on 
variational autoencoders (VAEs),
combining deep learning, probabilistic modelling and dynamical systems. 
Applications include
cell differentiation and glioma progression, with the goal of 
understanding how cells switch
between states and how these transitions change during tumour 
progression and treatment resistance.

Details about this internship are available upon request.

Host team — LPHI, University of Montpellier, CNRS, INSERM
An interdisciplinary team specialising in multiscale dynamical modelling 
of biological systems
(deterministic and probabilistic approaches), machine learning and 
artificial intelligence.

Partner team — IGF, Montpellier
A team specialising in gliomas, combining clinical data from 
neurosurgery (Prof. Hugues Duffau)
with multi-omics data and molecular neuroscience research (Prof. 
Jean-Philippe Hugnot).

Location: LPHI, University of Montpellier, CNRS, INSERM, Montpellier, France
Profile: Students in applied mathematics, computer science, machine 
learning or related fields.
